title: Consume pantheon-base-v0.17.7 into pantheon-ops
goal: Advance the Ops consumer from pantheon-base-v0.17.6 to the published pantheon-base-v0.17.7 so the tree inherits base's revive and CodeQL false-positive dispositions, repair the one remaining ops-owned goconst finding in the deploy package, and record the GitHub-side disposition that actually closes the nine open code scanning alerts on PR #149.
dependsOn: pantheon-base v0.17.7 release (tag object 6866fee0, target commit 2091a2d8)
blocks: ops branch and pull-request closeout to main only

in: Update foundation-release.lock.json to pantheon-base-v0.17.7: version, base commit, asset name, materialization path, bundle checksum and repo.tar checksum.
Rewrite .foundation/foundation-release.lock.json with the release identity and the Release Gate / Foundation Release Verify facts read back from GitHub.
Rebuild the Ops tree from the locked release snapshot, apply it, and re-tidy the merged Go module graph.
Name the repeated nginx service string in backend/modules/business/deploy so golangci-lint reports zero issues in the CI scope.
Dismiss the nine open code scanning alerts on the PR ref with per-alert reasons and re-run the PR feedback gate.
out: Any change to the pantheon-base repository, an existing tag, a published release or its assets.
Hand-copying base files into the Ops source tree instead of materializing the locked release.
Rewriting CHANGELOG.md or README*.md from base; those are Ops overlay paths by contract.
Any behaviour change in business modules beyond the goconst repair.
Rotating the SonarCloud token, and merging or closing the open Dependabot pull requests.

doNotTouch: any existing tag, release or release asset

implementationNotes: rebuild-from-base.mjs resolves the base from the lock when --base is omitted, so the round consumed the published v0.17.7 archive; the local Base checkout happens to sit on the same commit, which is what makes the against-main drift read meaningful.

go mod tidy reproduced go.mod and go.sum byte-identical to the v0.17.6 round, proving v0.17.7 moved no dependency; without the tidy the rebuild output reverts to Base's shorter indirect block and the tree does not build.

The inline // codeql annotations added in base v0.17.7 document the conclusion for a human reader but do not change GitHub alert state; alerts 56-64 stayed open until dismissed through the REST API, the same way 52 and 53 were in August.
Dismissals were applied by alert number, not line number, because the annotation comments shift lines while CodeQL's primaryLocationLineHash stays stable.
goconst counted seven occurrences of the nginx literal, four of them in production code; naming it once as defaultNginxServiceName removes all four and leaves only test fixtures.

consumerSpecificControls: release identity read back from GitHub instead of asserted from the bundle
code scanning disposition recorded per alert with its own reason
deferredCodeIssues: Ops business modules still create their schema through AutoMigrate instead of a consumer versioned-migration channel; no such channel exists in base
Runtime acceptance on a fresh database (startup plus golang-migrate to 000030) is still not executed in a consumer evidence set
the hosted SonarCloud Scan job fails with HTTP 403 from api.sonarcloud.io even though SONAR_TOKEN and SONAR_HOST_URL exist as repo secrets; needs a credential refresh, which is a maintainer action

designGate: inheritance boundary note: base owns the shared surface, ops consumes an immutable release snapshot and owns CHANGELOG/README overlays
developmentGate: rebuilt tree applied through the assembly, not by hand-copying
ops-owned lint finding fixed at its source
qaAcceptanceGate: business-overlay contract, shared-drift gate and 13 overlay tests on the applied tree
backend build/vet/gofmt/test on the tidied merged module graph
golangci-lint in the hosted CI scope reporting 0 issues
code scanning open-alert count zero repo-wide and the PR feedback gate passing locally

affectedSubgraph: foundation release -> consumer lock -> rebuilt tree -> shared surface files -> Go lint and code scanning gates
riskNodes: shared prefix of the ops tree

commands: go mod tidy && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l .
node scripts/check-encoding.mjs --strict && node scripts/harness/check-structure-contract.mjs --root . --strict && node scripts/frontmatter-check.mjs && node scripts/check-duplication.mjs
code scanning alert counts before and after the dismissal
runtimeEvidence: asset digests compared with the lock and the published .sha256 sidecars
sharedPaths deep-equality between the Ops lock and the manifest.json read out of the release tgz
golangci-lint run in the hosted scope on the repaired tree
GitHub code scanning open-alert count for the PR ref and repo-wide

costProfile.note: incremental release consumption; the only product change is one named constant

evidenceRequired: release identity and both asset digests re-hashed after materialization
sharedPaths equivalence between the Ops lock and the v0.17.7 release manifest
overlay contract, shared-drift and overlay test results on the applied tree
backend build/vet/gofmt/test and the CI-scoped golangci-lint result
the nine dismissed alert numbers with their reasons and the open count before and after
completionChecklist: Baseline advanced through the locked assembly
Code scanning disposition recorded per alert
